name: Carl Ford

items.text: In April 2013, Ford and Rep. Harry Warren filed House Joint Resolution 494. It said federal court rulings on government religious laws don't bind the state. They filed it amid a dispute over prayers at Rowan County meetings. The House Speaker's office said it was dead within days. Ford called the draft "poorly written" and said they were not starting a religion.
items.why: This was a legislative proposal that never came to a vote, and it shows no abuse of office, self-dealing or false statements about his record under any criterion, so it is a disputed stance rather than conduct.

for_review: Item 1's Wikipedia summary overstates the bill. WRAL and RNS describe a resolution asserting that federal court rulings on religious establishment don't bind the state, not a bill creating a state religion. Ford's response comes from RNS's account of a Salisbury Post interview. I didn't read the Salisbury Post original or the bill text on ncleg.gov. The one search on the owner's named sites (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) found nothing about this Carl Ford. I did no further searches on his donors, foreign ties, business record or other conduct, so nothing beyond this item was checked.
